title: aiops.diagnosis/v1
description: What the diagnosis agent must return for one incident (Phase 10d3). Structural rules live here; the rules that need state (every piece of evidence must correspond to a tool call the Toolbelt actually served for THIS incident, referenced runbooks/actions/docs must exist, no secrets) are enforced by aiops/toolbelt/diagnosis.py and are what makes the output checkable rather than trusted. A diagnosis PROPOSES; nothing in this document is ever executed.

incident_id.description: The Toolbelt incident this diagnosis is for.

layer.description: Where the fault most likely is: the guest/host itself, the hypervisor under it, the workload/app, the network path, drift from IaC, something external (cloud/DNS/ISP), or unknown (say so rather than guess).

summary.description: One short paragraph a human can act on.

reasoning.description: Why this layer: how the evidence rules the alternatives in or out.

evidence.description: Each item cites a tool call made for this incident. `layer` unknown may have none; every other layer needs at least one.

args.description: The arguments of that call, exactly as sent.

known_issue_refs.description: Repo docs that explain this failure class; each must exist.

proposed_actions.description: Registry actions a human could approve (10e). Proposals only.

action_id.description: Must be a key of aiops/actions.yml.

params.description: The registry extra-vars for this action (e.g. target_host, unit). Validated against the registry when the proposal is created; an invalid one is refused, not run.

needs_human.description: True when the agent could not narrow it down, or the fix is outside the action registry.
